name: pattern rules over blocks of typed values, in Haro (step 2 of COMPASS-REBOL-06/07), fixtures first
comment: Written BEFORE pattern_lib.haro. P01-P37 and X01-X16 are the study's 53, verbatim (study/rebol/pattern_fixtures.json); P38-P62 and X17-X37 are Haro's, each because no fixture pinned what it pins (the module docstring of gen_fixtures.py says which and why). A rule is C6 text, a list, read by the one LOAD (block_lib.haro); a grammar is data. Pattern words are UPPER_SNAKE keywords: the types WORD STRING NUMBER KEYWORD PATH PAIR LIST GROUP ROW OPTIONAL and SKIP (any one value); END; OPT ANY SOME REPEAT; OR (ordered choice); NOT AHEAD; INTO (a list, a group, a row, a pair read as its key then its value, an optional read as the value it marks); TO THRU; COLLECT KEEP; RULE name; MEMBER name (a value drawn from a SET the court collects, never code); LIT v. A lower_snake word, a string or a number in a rule matches itself. A rule matches only when it consumes its whole input. THE BOUND, refused at declaration and never at match time: recursion, a repetition or TO over a rule that can match nothing, a group in a rule, WHILE DO EVAL IF, and the editing words CHANGE INSERT REMOVE. Matching is PEG with a packrat memo: at most (rule nodes x input positions) steps, held on every match fixture. "matches" are judged by the verdict and the values kept; "refusals" by the fragment of why the declaration is refused. "family" is judged over every declaration and sentence of the spike, by the number that match and the six that do not, by name. Every fixture is judged on haro and its checked build, byte-identical, and beside the Python reference (study/rebol/pattern.py), the two refusing a difference by name (D43).

matches.name: a sequence of types
the same sequence, out of order, does not match
OPT: a value that may be absent
ANY then END: every value is a word
ANY then END: a number stops it short of the end
SOME needs at least one
OR: ordered choice, the second alternative taken
literal words as a closed menu: a word outside it does not match
literal words as a closed menu: a word inside it matches
LIT matches a keyword as itself (a bare keyword in a rule is a pattern word)
INTO descends into a list: every item a word
INTO: a number among the items does not match
a declaration's shape: DEFINE, its kind, its name, AS, a group of rows, RATIONALE and a string

matches.name: a clause is a row of a keyword and one value
a bare string where a clause belongs is not a row
PAIR: a seat list is pairs
INTO a pair reads it as its key and its value
MEMBER: a value drawn from a declared set
MEMBER: a value outside the set does not match

the value join (stzzui's VIBE_STRIPS_RIGHT): every strip is a value some other declaration's list seat holds -- the set is the union of those seats, which the court collects as data and the rule only reads
COLLECT and KEEP: the words kept, the numbers passed over
KEEP outside a COLLECT keeps into the result
TO skips up to what matches, consuming none of it
THRU skips past what matches
NOT: a value that is not a number, every time
NOT: a number stops it
AHEAD looks without consuming
REPEAT n: exactly two words
REPEAT n: three words are one too many
REPEAT n m: between one and two
named rules, referred to and never recursive
a comment is not a value
INTO, three deep
an empty list
a path is one value
items are values, a row is one item: [a b, c] is two items, the first a row
ordered choice commits: the first alternative that matches is taken, and the rest is not tried again
OPTIONAL: the mark `?` makes one value of its own kind (Q-B1)
a plain word is not an OPTIONAL
an optional value is not a WORD: the mark is part of the value
INTO an optional descends into the value it makes optional
INTO an optional list, one level further
a declaration's seat list: a pair of a name and a type, a list of types, or either made optional

a rule matches only when it consumes its whole input

a named rule used twice in one rule
a sub-rule is a sequence in its place
a pair is one value; its key is read as a word
